subfamily: Stone Fence (spirit and hard cider, Oxford STONE FENCE pdf 1931), kept still and sharp: aged rum lengthened with dry, still farmhouse cider over two or three small lumps of ice (the ice as Jerry Thomas asked, 1862, Imbibe! pdf 160; never his recipe)
glass: heavy tumbler (about 300 ml), two or three small lumps of ice
version: v1.2 (Tomás, round 4 step 1, 2026-10-04; drink unchanged since v1, round 2). Rum : cider 3:8 (45:120). Oxford's colonial 'roughly equal' runs 22.8%, OUT of the highball band; 1:2 at 50:100 sat on the edge (17.0%) and a 43% rum sent it OUT, so the cider was lengthened toward Jerry Thomas's 'fill up the glass' (Imbibe! pdf 160). No sugar: Oxford STONE FENCE (pdf 1931) mentions sugar only for the times it was served hot (Hester A6). The fruit goes in raw: a thin slice of the sharpest apple to hand, cut last. Never apple brandy (the Lover family's bottle).
